Apple Pencil USB-C — The Most Compatible Apple Pencil for iPad

The Apple Pencil USB-C is Apple's most accessible and most widely compatible stylus. With pixel-perfect precision, tilt sensitivity and low latency, the Apple Pencil USB-C makes note-taking, signing documents and drawing easy at an affordable entry point. It pairs and charges via USB-C and magnetically attaches to iPad. For Pakistani students, professionals and everyday iPad users who want a stylus for writing, annotating and sketching without the advanced features of the Pro model, the Apple Pencil USB-C is the right starting point.

Who This Is For

The Apple Pencil USB-C is built for three groups of people. Students who want to take handwritten notes, annotate lecture slides and fill in digital worksheets. Professionals who need to sign documents, mark up PDFs and annotate presentations on their iPad throughout the workday. And first-time Apple Pencil buyers who want to experience the precision of an Apple stylus without committing to the full Pro feature set.

If you are a digital artist who paints or sketches seriously and relies on pressure-sensitive brush strokes that vary based on how hard you press, the Apple Pencil Pro or 2nd generation model is the better fit. The biggest practical difference for artists is simple: Apple Pencil Pro, Apple Pencil 2nd generation and Apple Pencil 1st generation support pressure-sensitive drawing. Apple Pencil USB-C does not. That one difference matters more than most spec lists. For everything else, the USB-C Pencil delivers the Apple Pencil experience fully.

iPad Compatibility

Apple Pencil USB-C works with iPad Pro 13-inch M4 and M5, iPad Pro 12.9-inch 3rd through 6th generation, iPad Pro 11-inch M4 and M5, iPad Pro 11-inch 1st through 4th generation, iPad Air 13-inch M2, M3 and M4, iPad Air 11-inch M2 and M3, iPad Air 4th and 5th generation, iPad A16, iPad mini A17 Pro, iPad mini 6th generation and iPad 10th generation. In simple terms, if your iPad has a USB-C port and was released from 2018 onward, the Apple Pencil USB-C almost certainly works with it. This is the widest compatibility of any Apple Pencil model.

iPad Compatibility

iPad Pro 13-inch (M4 and M5) iPad Pro 11-inch (M4 and M5) iPad Pro 11-inch (1st, 2nd, 3rd, or 4th generation) iPad Pro 12.9-inch (3rd, 4th, 5th or 6th generation) iPad Air 13-inch (M2, M3, and M4) iPad Air 11-inch (M2, M3, and M4) iPad Air (4th or 5th generation) iPad (A16) iPad (10th generation) iPad mini (A17 Pro) iPad mini (6th generation)

Key Features

Pixel-Perfect Precision and Low Latency

Apple Pencil USB-C is perfect for taking notes, sketching, marking up documents, journaling and more. It delivers pixel-perfect precision, low latency and tilt sensitivity. So it is as natural to use as a pencil. Every stroke appears the moment you make it with no visible lag. Writing in Notes, annotating a PDF, marking up a presentation or sketching a diagram all feel immediate and accurate.

Tilt Sensitivity for Natural Shading

All Apple Pencils provide tilt and rotation detection while drawing. Tilt the Apple Pencil USB-C to the side and supported apps respond with a wider, softer stroke just like shading with the side of a pencil on paper. For students drawing diagrams, architects sketching layouts and anyone creating visual notes, tilt sensitivity makes the experience significantly more natural than any basic capacitive stylus available at similar price points in Pakistan.

Hover Detection on iPad Pro and iPad Air

When used with M2 models of iPad Pro, the new Apple Pencil supports hover, allowing users to sketch and illustrate with even greater precision. Bring the Pencil tip close to the screen without touching it and compatible apps show a preview of exactly where your next mark will appear. In note-taking apps, a cursor appears before you touch down. In drawing apps, you see a preview of your tool before committing the stroke. Hover makes fine placement significantly more precise, particularly for small handwriting and detailed annotations.

USB-C Charging and Pairing

A sliding cap reveals a USB-C port, enabling customers to use a USB-C cable to connect to the Apple Pencil for pairing and charging. Slide the cap to reveal the port, connect any USB-C cable and the Pencil charges and pairs. The same cable used by your iPhone, iPad or MacBook works. No separate adapter, no wireless alignment required. For Pakistani users who carry one USB-C charger for multiple devices, this is the most straightforward charging experience of any Apple Pencil model.

Magnetic Attachment for Storage

Designed with a matte finish and a flat side that magnetically attaches to the side of iPad for storage, the new Apple Pencil enters into a sleep state to preserve battery life when magnetically attached. The Pencil snaps securely to the side of the iPad when not in use and enters sleep mode automatically to preserve battery. Note that it does not charge wirelessly through this magnetic connection — pairing and charging require the USB-C cable.

Works With Apple Intelligence and iPadOS Features

The new Apple Pencil works great with iPadOS features like Scribble, Quick Note and when collaborating with others in Freeform. Scribble converts your handwriting to typed text anywhere you can type on the iPad. Quick Note lets you jot down notes instantly from any screen with a swipe gesture. Freeform lets you collaborate on a shared whiteboard in real time. All of these work fully with the Apple Pencil USB-C.

Apple Pencil USB-C vs Apple Pencil Pro

Both are genuine Apple Pencils with pixel-perfect precision and low latency. The USB-C model is the right choice for note-taking, document annotation and everyday iPad use across the widest range of iPad models. The Apple Pencil Pro is the right choice for digital artists who need pressure sensitivity, squeeze gestures for instant tool switching, barrel roll for brush orientation, haptic feedback and Find My support. If you use your iPad primarily for written work and document annotation, the USB-C Pencil covers everything you need. If you use Procreate, Adobe Fresco or any creative drawing app professionally, the Pro is the better investment.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does the Apple Pencil USB-C have pressure sensitivity?

The Apple Pencil USB-C does not support pressure sensitivity, which is even supported on the first-generation Apple Pencil. This makes it less ideal for artists. For note-taking, document annotation, signing and casual sketching, this is not a limitation in practice. For serious digital art where varying brush weight through pressure is essential, the Apple Pencil Pro is the better choice.

Which iPads is the Apple Pencil USB-C compatible with?

Apple Pencil USB-C works with iPad Pro 13-inch M4 and M5, iPad Pro 12.9-inch 3rd through 6th generation, iPad Pro 11-inch M4 and M5 and 1st through 4th generation, iPad Air 13-inch M2 M3 and M4, iPad Air 11-inch M2 and M3, iPad Air 4th and 5th generation, iPad A16, iPad mini A17 Pro, iPad mini 6th generation and iPad 10th generation. It is the most widely compatible Apple Pencil available.

Does the Apple Pencil USB-C charge wirelessly on the iPad?

No. While it can connect to an iPad magnetically, it does not pair and charge wirelessly. It must be charged via the included USB-C port. The magnetic attachment keeps the Pencil on the side of your iPad for storage and puts it into sleep mode to preserve battery, but does not charge it. Charging requires connecting the USB-C cable to the sliding cap at the top of the Pencil.

What is the difference between the Apple Pencil USB-C and the Apple Pencil Pro?

The Apple Pencil Pro adds pressure sensitivity, squeeze gesture for instant tool switching, barrel roll using the built-in gyroscope, haptic feedback and Find My support. It also charges and pairs wirelessly through magnetic attachment. The Apple Pencil USB-C has tilt sensitivity and hover detection but no pressure sensitivity, no squeeze, no barrel roll, no haptics and no Find My. The Pro also works only with the newest iPad models from 2024 onward, while the USB-C works with almost every iPad that has a USB-C port.

Can I use the Apple Pencil USB-C for drawing in Procreate?

Yes, but with limitations. The USB-C Pencil can work for drawing if you are on a budget, but it is more suited to note-taking and browsing. Tilt sensitivity works in Procreate for shading effects. However, the lack of pressure sensitivity means brush size and opacity cannot be controlled by pressing harder — all strokes come out at uniform pressure. For casual sketching and illustration, it works. For professional digital art where pressure variation is central to the workflow, the Apple Pencil Pro delivers a significantly better experience.

How do I check which Apple Pencil is compatible with my iPad?

Go to Settings on your iPad, tap General, then About, and note your Model Name. Check your iPad model first before buying any Apple Pencil, as compatibility varies significantly between models. The Vision Tech team at the Clifton showroom can also check compatibility for you in person before purchase.

Does Vision Tech deliver the Apple Pencil USB-C outside Karachi?

Yes. Nationwide delivery covers Lahore, Islamabad, Rawalpindi, Faisalabad, Multan, Peshawar, Hyderabad and all major cities. Cash on Delivery is available for most locations. Contact Vision Tech directly for current stock and delivery timelines before ordering.

Apple Pencil Pro — The Most Advanced Apple Stylus Ever Made

The Apple Pencil Pro is Apple's most capable stylus and the first meaningful upgrade to the Apple Pencil formula in years. Apple Pencil Pro adds even more magical capabilities to help bring your ideas to life. Advanced features like squeeze, barrel roll and haptic feedback make marking up, taking notes and creating a masterpiece more intuitive than ever. It is the right choice for digital artists, designers, architects, illustrators and any iPad user who wants the complete, unrestricted Apple Pencil experience on a compatible iPad.

Compatibility — Important to Check Before Buying

Apple Pencil Pro works with iPad Pro 13-inch M4 and M5, iPad Pro 11-inch M4 and M5, iPad Air 11-inch M2, M3 and M4, iPad Air 13-inch M2, M3 and M4 and iPad mini A17 Pro. The Apple Pencil Pro works only with iPad models released from 2024 onward with M2, M3, M4 or M5 chips. If you own an older iPad, check your model name in Settings before purchasing. The Vision Tech team at the Clifton showroom can confirm compatibility with your specific iPad before you buy. You can use Apple Pencil Pro only with these iPad models and iPadOS 17.5 or later: iPad Pro 13-inch (M4 and M5) iPad Pro 11-inch (M4 and M5) iPad Air 13-inch (M2, M3, and M4) iPad Air 11-inch (M2, M3, and M4) iPad mini (A17 Pro)

Squeeze — Switch Tools Without Lifting the Pencil

Apple Pencil Pro can sense when you squeeze it and brings up a new palette so you can quickly switch tools, line weights and colors, thanks to a new sensor. In Procreate, a squeeze opens the tool picker so you can change from a brush to an eraser, switch colours or adjust line weight without ever putting the Pencil down or reaching for the screen with your other hand. In Notes, a squeeze opens an undo and redo slider. In Adobe Fresco, it opens a shortcut toolbar with recent brushes and colour adjustments.

The squeeze is customisable. In the Settings app under Apple Pencil, you choose what the squeeze gesture triggers — the default tool palette, colour picker, Eyedropper or Quick Shape. A sensitivity slider adjusts how firm the squeeze needs to be, which makes it accessible for users who want a lighter activation or need an accessibility-friendly input.

Barrel Roll — Rotate the Brush Like a Real Pen

A new gyroscope allows you to rotate Apple Pencil Pro for precise control of shaped pen and brush tools. In practice, this is one of the most genuinely useful advances in the Apple Pencil Pro for digital artists. When you use a shaped brush or calligraphy pen in Procreate, the orientation of that brush in the app tracks the physical rotation of the Pencil in your hand. Rotate the Pencil clockwise and the brush tool rotates clockwise on screen. This mirrors exactly how a real calligraphy pen, a flat-tipped marker or an angled brush works in the physical world. For calligraphers, lettering artists and illustrators working with directional brushes in Pakistan's growing digital art community, this feature fundamentally changes how naturally creative tools behave on screen.

Haptic Feedback — Feel Every Action Confirmed

A custom haptic engine provides precise feedback you can feel. When you squeeze or double tap, you will feel a light pulse confirming the action. Haptics close the gap between digital and physical drawing in a way that is difficult to describe until you feel it. When a shape snaps to a Smart Shape guide in Notes, you feel the confirmation. When you squeeze to open the tool palette, a tactile pulse confirms the gesture registered. When you double-tap to switch tools, the feedback makes the interaction feel deliberate and physical rather than abstract and screen-only. It turns what can sometimes feel like a disconnected experience into a more natural, tactile one.

Pressure Sensitivity — The Foundation of Expressive Drawing

Apple Pencil Pro features pixel-perfect precision, tilt and pressure sensitivity and low latency. Pressure sensitivity means the harder you press, the darker and wider the brush stroke. The lighter you press, the softer and thinner it appears. This is the fundamental mechanic of all expressive drawing — the same mechanic that makes a pencil on paper respond to your hand pressure. Without pressure sensitivity, digital art lacks this expressiveness. The Apple Pencil Pro restores it fully, making every stroke you draw on screen respond to your intent in the same way a real pencil or brush would on paper.

Find My — Never Lose Your Pencil

Find My is available for the Apple Pencil Pro so it can be tracked right alongside the iPad and other devices in the Find My app. The Apple Pencil Pro communicates its last known location through the Find My network via Bluetooth. If you misplace it at home, in a studio, at a university or in an office, open Find My on your iPhone or iPad and its last known location appears on the map. For creative professionals in Pakistan who carry their Apple Pencil Pro to client meetings, classes or shared workspaces, Find My provides genuine peace of mind that a lost Pencil can be located.

Double Tap — Instant Tool Switching

Use double tap to quickly switch between tools, like a pen and an eraser. A double tap on the flat side of the Pencil switches between your current tool and the last used tool — typically between a drawing tool and the eraser. For correcting mistakes during a drawing session, double tap is faster than any other method of reaching the eraser and switching back. Combined with squeeze for the full tool palette and barrel roll for orientation, the Apple Pencil Pro gives you more gesture controls than any other stylus on any platform.

Hover Detection With Tool Shadow

Use Apple Pencil hover to preview exactly where Apple Pencil Pro will touch down on your display and see a virtual shadow of your tool. The hover shadow is unique to the Apple Pencil Pro. Whatever tool you have selected — a calligraphy brush, a marker, a stamp tool — its shape appears as a rendered shadow on screen as you hover. This shows you not just where the Pencil will land but the exact orientation and shape of the mark it will make before you commit to the stroke. For precise illustration and detailed digital work, this level of preview eliminates placement errors entirely.

Magnetic Wireless Charging and Pairing

Apple Pencil Pro attaches, charges and pairs magnetically on the side of compatible iPads. Attach the Pencil to the side of your iPad and it pairs automatically and begins charging wirelessly. No cable, no cap, no port. Remove it and it is ready to draw. The magnetic connection is secure enough to keep the Pencil on the iPad during normal movement without sliding off. This is the most convenient charging system of any Apple Pencil model.

Transforms iPad Into a Complete Creative Studio

Draw, sketch, colour, take notes and mark up documents. Use built-in apps like Notes and Freeform, or choose from over a million more apps available on the App Store. Procreate, Adobe Fresco, Affinity Designer and every other major creative app on the App Store fully supports the Apple Pencil Pro's squeeze, barrel roll, pressure sensitivity and haptic features. For Pakistani designers, illustrators, architects, fashion designers and digital artists, the iPad Pro with Apple Pencil Pro is a professional creative tool that replaces a drawing tablet and stylus setup at a fraction of the combined cost.

Frequently Asked Questions

Which iPads are compatible with the Apple Pencil Pro?

Apple Pencil Pro works with iPad Pro 13-inch M4 and M5, iPad Pro 11-inch M4 and M5, iPad Air 11-inch M2, M3 and M4, iPad Air 13-inch M2, M3 and M4 and iPad mini A17 Pro. It does not work with older iPad models or any iPad with an M1 chip or earlier. Always check your iPad model in Settings before purchasing.

What is the squeeze gesture and how do I use it?

Apple Pencil Pro can sense when you squeeze it and brings up a new palette so you can quickly switch tools, line weights and colors. In Procreate, squeeze opens the tool picker. In Notes, it opens the undo and redo history slider. In Adobe Fresco, it opens a shortcut toolbar. The squeeze action and its function can be customised in Settings under Apple Pencil. A sensitivity slider adjusts how firm the squeeze needs to be to activate.

What is barrel roll and which apps support it?

A new gyroscope allows you to rotate Apple Pencil Pro for precise control of shaped pen and brush tools. When you physically rotate the Pencil in your hand, the orientation of the selected brush or tool on screen rotates to match. Apps that support barrel roll include Procreate, Notes, Freeform and any app built with PencilKit or that has added Apple Pencil Pro support. The list of compatible apps grows continuously as developers update their apps.

Does the Apple Pencil Pro work with Procreate?

Yes. Procreate fully supports all Apple Pencil Pro features including pressure sensitivity, tilt, barrel roll, squeeze and haptic feedback. With squeeze, you can maintain a continuous flow of drawing and colour sampling without adjusting your grip. The haptic feedback responds to squeezing the Apple Pencil and turns what can feel like a disconnected experience into a more natural tactile one. For Pakistani digital artists using Procreate, the Apple Pencil Pro is the best stylus available for that app.

How does Find My work on the Apple Pencil Pro?

Find My is available for the Apple Pencil Pro so it can be tracked right alongside the iPad and other devices in the Find My app. The Pencil broadcasts a Bluetooth signal that the Find My network uses to determine its last known location. Open Find My on your iPhone and the Apple Pencil Pro appears alongside your other devices and AirTags. If the Pencil is in Bluetooth range, Precision Finding can guide you to it directly. If it is out of range, the last known location is shown on the map.

Does the Apple Pencil Pro charge wirelessly?

Yes. Apple Pencil Pro attaches, charges and pairs magnetically on the side of compatible iPads. Attach the Pencil magnetically to the side of your compatible iPad and it charges automatically with no cable required. Remove it and it is ready to use. No separate charging case, cable or adapter is needed for daily charging.

Is the Apple Pencil Pro compatible with older iPad Pro models?

No. The Apple Pencil Pro requires M4 or M5 iPad Pro models released in 2024 or later. It only works with 13-inch iPad Pro M4 and M5, 11-inch iPad Pro M4 and M5, M2 and M3 iPad Airs and iPad mini A17 Pro. If you own an iPad Pro with an M1, M2 or M3 chip, the Apple Pencil 2nd generation is the compatible stylus for that device. The Vision Tech team can confirm which Pencil works with your specific iPad before you purchase.

What is the difference between the Apple Pencil Pro and the Apple Pencil USB-C?

The Apple Pencil Pro adds pressure sensitivity, squeeze gesture, barrel roll gyroscope, haptic feedback, Find My support and wireless magnetic charging and pairing. It works only with the newest iPad models from 2024 onward. The Apple Pencil USB-C has tilt sensitivity and hover detection but no pressure sensitivity, no squeeze, no barrel roll, no haptics and no Find My. It charges via the USB-C port and works with the widest range of iPads. Choose the Pro if you are a digital artist or want every feature. Choose the USB-C if you primarily take notes and annotate documents on an older or more widely compatible iPad.
